Memo submitted. Here are the numbers:

## US March 2026 Revenue by Stream

| Stream | GL | USD |
|---|---|---|
| Subscription | 4000 | 52,300.00 |
| Usage | 4100 | 977.00 |
| Professional services | 4200 | 7,500.00 |
| **Total** | | **60,777.00** |

**The trail** — seven posted AR entries, all with support attached:

- **Subscription 52,300** = five March 1 invoices (JE-00222 Acme 18,000 / JE-00224 Corvid 11,500 / JE-00219 Fairview 9,400 / JE-00215 Beacon 8,000 / JE-00225 Evergreen 6,200 = 53,100 gross) less JE-00275, the 800 Beacon SLA credit memo.
- **Usage 977** = JE-00236, INV-2180 Acme API overage.
- **Prof services 7,500** = JE-00255, INV-2118 Fairview implementation.

I changed nothing in the books — read-only throughout.

**Three things worth knowing before this goes to the CFO:**

1. **Usage revenue is billed a month in arrears.** The 977 in March is *February* consumption. Applied consistently across all three months, so trending is valid, but don't label it "March usage" in a board deck.

2. **The only reason subscription dips below Jan/Feb is the SLA credit.** Underlying recurring billings are flat at 53,100 all quarter; the 800 credit relates to a *February* incident but was booked 3/20. Immaterial, left as posted, but it explains the entire variance.

3. **"Revenue recognition" is still an open checklist item** for US March. Everything above ties and is fully supported, but treat it as preliminary until the revenue accountant signs off.

I also ran completeness work rather than just reading the three account balances: all 13 AR-side entries scanned (the other 6 are cash receipts with no P&L effect); deferred revenue, unbilled receivables, suspense, and unapplied cash are all nil so nothing is hiding off-stream; all five recurring customers were invoiced; and all three accounts roll forward exactly to their cumulative balances. One apparent duplicate — two Acme invoices both citing "February 2026" usage — cleared as a mislabeled description on the February invoice, not a double-count.
